title: The Claude app and its plans

opening.headline: When the Claude app, API, and Claude Code are all called 'Claude' and you can't tell them apart, learn how to read the products separately and compare the management differences in the plans.
body: Claude, which talks in a chat window, the API that developers call with code to create services, and Claude Code, which handles the code base in the terminal, are all called the same name. Since the names are the same, it is difficult to tell where and which one is used for my work.

In this class, we will first discuss the characteristics of the three products and then check the methods and limits for uploading files in the Claude app. Next, we compare how the individual plan, team, and enterprise plan differ in management method rather than functionality, and explain the difference when solving the same needs with individual subscription and team plan.
objectives: Can explain the distinction between Claude App, API, and Claude Code
You can distinguish between management of individual, team, and corporate plans.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: They're all 'Claude' but they're different
screens.lead: Let's look at three things that go by the same name. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

visual.alt: Mockup with app, API, and Claude Code split under one Claude logo.

items.prompt: Claude app talking in chat window
items.answer: This is a product that communicates on the web, desktop, and mobile. People ask questions, upload files, and edit posts directly on the screen.

items.prompt: API that developers call with code
items.answer: This is a method where developers create their own service by directly calling the model with code. The Claude Platform documentation introduces the Messages API for granular control and Claude Managed Agents running on a managed infrastructure.

items.prompt: Claude Code dealing with the code base from the terminal
items.answer: A coding assistant who understands your codebase and works across multiple files and tools. You can use it in terminal, IDE, desktop, and web.

Because all three products are called the same name, it is difficult to tell where they are used. It is much easier if you first understand that each product has different users, screens, and management methods.

screens.outro: First, let's think about what screen I use Claude on.

screens.title: Think about it: What screen do I use on?
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: What screen are you using Claude on?
items.answer: Most people meet Claude in the chat window of their browser or through the desktop or mobile app. That screen is the Claude app. Developers may encounter the same service differently in code or terminal.
Web, desktop, and mobile are all the same app family, and the tool used in the terminal is Claude Code. Keep in mind that different screens may require different products.

items.prompt: Have you ever uploaded a file or shared it with a team member?
items.answer: File uploads and team use are where the differences between the apps and plans are most apparent. The second half of this lesson covers just this. In most cases, you can tell which product is being used just by distinguishing between the screens.

screens.outro: Now let's take a look at file uploads in the Claude app.

screens.title: Claude app and file upload
screens.lead: If you hover over or select an underlined term in the following article, an explanation will appear. Check the file upload method and limits.

visual.alt: Model screen showing the file add menu in the Claude input window
labels: Chat: 500MB per file, 20 per chat / Project: 30MB per file

data.text: The Claude app is a conversational product available on web, desktop, and mobile platforms. By tapping the + button in the lower-left corner of the input field and selecting Add files or photos, you can choose a file from your device and drag it into the chat window. The app supports PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON, and XLSX file types for documents, and JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP for images. You can upload up to 500MB files per chat session and up to 20 files per chat. In contrast, project files have a limit of 30MB per file. The upload limits vary depending on the destination where the file is being uploaded.

terms.tip: This is a menu item that appears when you press the + button in the input window. Select a file from your device and attach it. You can also paste an image from the clipboard.
You can upload Excel files only if you turn on code execution and file creation in your account. This is a representative example of different document formats and different conditions.
This is the size limit for a single file uploaded to chat. Images can be up to 8000x8000 pixels wide and tall, and PDFs can be up to 1000 pages.
This is the maximum number of files that can be posted in one chat. To repeatedly write more material, use the file area of ​​your project.
This is the size limit for project files. There is no limit to the number, but the entire content must fit within Claude's context window, and text extraction is standard.

screens.outro: Now that you've seen how to upload a file, let's look at the distinction between products and plans.

screens.title: Plan system and product classification
screens.lead: Select each tab to see how they differ between Personal Plan, Team and Enterprise Plan, and API and Claude Code.

tabs.label: personal plan
tabs.body: Personal plans are divided into Free, Pro, and Max. Free lets you chat on the web, desktop, and mobile, search the web, create files, run code, use memory, and use Artifacts. Pro offers everything in Free plus more usage, Projects, Claude Code, and more Claude models. Max offers 5x or 20x more usage than Pro, higher output limits, and priority access during high traffic hours.

tabs.label: Team Plan
tabs.body: The Team plan is a paid plan for teams. It provides all the features of Pro plus administrator tools and central billing management, SSO and domain capture, role-based permissions, organizational and individual spending limits, and enterprise search. Usage limits apply to each member rather than the entire team, so if one person reaches their limit, others can continue to use. Up to 150 seats are supported.

tabs.label: Enterprise
tabs.body: Enterprise is the plan for larger organizations and provides the management capabilities of Team plus security and management features such as SCIM, audit logs, usage analytics, Compliance API, and custom data retention controls. Organizations that exceed the 150 seats supported by the Team plan can move to Enterprise. The key point is that who controls access and records is more important than the name of the function.

tabs.label: API
tabs.body: An API is a way for developers to call models directly with code. The Claude Platform documentation introduces two methods: The Messages API is ideal for custom agent loops and granular control by sending prompts directly to models. Claude Managed Agents are a configurable agent framework running on a managed infrastructure, ideal for long-running asynchronous tasks. We advise you to manage your API keys by setting an expiration date rather than putting them in the source code or prompt.

tabs.label: Claude Code
tabs.body: Claude Code is a coding assistant that understands your code base and works across multiple files and tools from your terminal. It is included in Pro, Max, and Team plans and can be used in IDE, desktop, and web in addition to terminal. Since it is a tool for developers who write code, you can use the Claude app for general document work.

screens.outro: Now that we've divided the products and plans, let's address the same request in two ways.

screens.title: Explanatory example: Same needs as individual subscription and team plan
screens.lead: The instructor explains the difference between solving the same needs with an individual subscription and a team plan. Select the next arrow to follow the comparison.

steps.title: read request
steps.body: The request is, ‘I want five people to write reports using the same data, and I want to manage usage and costs in one place.’ The features you need are conversation, file upload, and data sharing. This is something you can try with either an individual subscription or a team plan, but the results vary greatly. The criterion for judgment is not ‘whether it functions,’ but ‘who manages it and how.’

steps.title: Step 1: If you unlock with a personal subscription
steps.body: If five people each subscribe to Pro, they each use the Claude app with their own account and payment. Although the functionality is sufficient, usage is also managed separately for each person. It's difficult to see at a glance who is spending how much, and data is scattered across individual chats and projects. Even if there is a resignation or personnel change, it is difficult for the organization to collect the account. Since costs are paid individually, it is difficult for the organization to determine the total amount. For this reason, when several people work on the same task, management methods are considered first. This is the starting point of the case.

steps.title: Step 2: Solve it with a team plan
steps.body: The Team plan puts admin tools and billing management in one place. Owners can manage access and billing and set spending limits on an organizational and individual basis. If you want to use more, you can turn on usage credits to continue working beyond your limit.

steps.title: Step 3: Control access
steps.body: Team Plan controls who writes what with SSO, domain capture, and role-based permissions. Each member has a separate limit, so even if one person uses a lot, it does not affect the usage of others. The seat is reserved for one named person and the limit cannot be shared with another person.

steps.title: Step 4: Feature must be turned on by the owner
steps.body: On the Team plan, features like web browsing also depend on organization-wide settings. The owner must turn it on at the organization level for members to use it. Individual subscriptions are turned on by the user, but in teams, the setting is up to the organization. Connection functions such as connectors are also used under administrator control.

steps.title: Step 5: Check file and data limits
steps.body: Either way, file limits follow the same principles. Upload 500MB per file for chat, up to 20 files per chat, and place materials that will be used repeatedly in multiple conversations in a project to adhere to the 30MB limit per file. It is better to divide large documents and handle them within limits. Please note that PDFs exceeding 100 pages will only be analyzed for text and visual elements will not be visible, and PDFs exceeding 1000 pages cannot be uploaded. If the PDF has important pictures, it is best to divide it into 100 pages or less.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: The difference between the two approaches is not in the name of the feature, but in how it is managed. Individual subscriptions are managed individually, while team plan owners manage access, billing, spending limits, and permissions in one place. If the requirement is to ‘write well alone’, then the individual plan is appropriate, and if the requirement is ‘to write with multiple people under control’, then the team plan is appropriate.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the difference in management methods through examples, we will summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Summary: Different products under the same name
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Read this while remembering which product your work belongs to.

paragraphs: Claude App is a product that a person interacts with on a screen, API is how developers call models with code, and Claude Code is a coding assistant that handles the code base. The starting point for this class was that there were different products under the same name.

Personal, team, and enterprise plans differ in how they are managed rather than their list of features. The Personal plan is for individual use, Team adds central billing, permission controls, and spending limits, and Enterprise adds security and management features like audit logs and SCIM.
File upload limits are different for chat and projects. Chats are 20 chats at 500MB per file, and projects are 30MB per file. Keep in mind that your limits will vary depending on where you post.
The API and Claude Code are for developers. If it's a general task, start with the Claude app, if code is the core, think of Claude Code, and if you create your own service, think of the API.

Lastly, keep in mind that team plan usage limits apply to each member, and one person's usage doesn't affect anyone else's limits. When usage exceeds the limit and needs to continue, the owner can turn on usage credits.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: To upload XLSX files, you must turn on code execution and file creation on your account. If upload does not work, check the file format and this setting together.

glossary.def: This is a Claude product that speaks on the web, desktop, and mobile.
This method allows developers to send prompts directly to the model, and is used when detailed control is required.
A coding assistant who understands your codebase and works across multiple files and tools.
Paid plan for teams with admin tools, central billing, permission controls, and spending limits.
This feature allows Claude to reference documents and images by attaching them to a chat or project.

misconceptions.myth: There is only one place where Claude is used.
misconceptions.fact: The Claude App, API, and Claude Code are different products. Each user, screen, and management method is different.

misconceptions.myth: When the plan goes up, it becomes a completely different AI.
misconceptions.fact: What varies by plan are model access, usage, and management features. The differences between Team and Enterprise plans lie specifically in management practices such as access control, billing, and auditing.

misconceptions.myth: File upload limits are the same everywhere.
misconceptions.fact: You can upload up to 500 MB per file in chat, up to 20 files per chat, and 30 MB per file in project files. Each posting location has different limits.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: There are different products under the same name. Apps are conversations, APIs are developer calls, and Claude Code is a tool for working with code.
Individual, team, and enterprise plans differ in management style rather than functionality.
File upload limits are different for chat and projects.
The API and Claude Code are for developers.

Products that talk on the web, desktop, and mobile

checks.explain: Even though they have the same Claude name, the conversation products, developer calls, code work tools, and managed plans are different.
checks.intro: There are several products and methods under the Claude name as well. Match items with descriptions.
checks.correctFeedback: That's correct. You've distinguished that apps, API calls, code tools, and plans are different things.
checks.incorrectFeedback: There is a mismatched pair. Divide into plans that offer interactive products, developer-directed calls, code-working tools, and management tools.

checks.q: I want five people to write reports using the same data and manage usage in one place. How is a team plan different from an individual subscription?

Owners manage access, billing and spending limits in one place
Each person pays separately and manages their usage individually.
Web browsing is automatically turned on for all members
checks.explain: The difference lies in the management method rather than the function name. Team owners set access, billing, and spending limits and control them with SSO and role permissions.

wrong.0: The difference is not the feature name, but the way it is managed.
wrong.2: It is a method of personal subscription.
wrong.3: Web search can only be used by members if the owner turns it on for the entire organization.

checks.intro: See how team plans differ from individual subscriptions.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. The difference is not functionality, but management: Owners manage access, billing, and spending limits in one place.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The difference isn't the new features or automatically turned on searches, but the way you manage them. Pay attention to who sets access and costs.
